cards.a: The minute or microscopic structural and functional unit of the kidney.

cards.q: Which two components compose a nephron?
cards.a: A renal corpuscle and a renal tubule.

cards.q: What does the renal corpuscle consist of?
cards.a: A tuft of capillaries called a glomerulus and a cup-shaped structure called Bowman's capsule.
The interior of Bowman's capsule, which collects the filtrate from the filtering capillaries of the glomerular tuft.

cards.q: What are Bowman's capsule and the renal tubule composed of?
Which two sections make up the proximal tubule?
cards.a: A convoluted section (proximal convoluted tubule) followed by a straight section (proximal straight tubule).

cards.q: What are the two parts of the loop of Henle?
cards.a: The descending loop of Henle and the ascending loop of Henle.

cards.q: Through which three layers is blood filtered in the nephron?
cards.a: The endothelial cells of the capillary wall, its basement membrane, and between the podocyte foot processes of the capsule lining.

cards.q: Which cells support the capillaries of the glomerular tuft?
What happens to water as fluid from Bowman's capsule flows down the tubule?
cards.a: It is reabsorbed, while substances are exchanged by the epithelial cells lining the tubule.

cards.q: What does the processing of tubular fluid regulate?
cards.a: The volume of body fluid as well as levels of many body substances.
